text:
marina: FYI Nimbus Labs sent their standard open-model license for NLX-3. They have a clause that explicitly allows API integrations but prohibits hosting the model weights or packaging in marketplaces. Can we get a carve-out?
ajay: Paste the clause? If it's 'no hosting' that's going to block any Redwood marketplace SKU and Dedicated images.
marina: Here it is verbatim:
```
No Hosting or Redistribution: The Licensee may access the Model via Provider-hosted APIs only. Licensee shall not host, mirror, redistribute, sublicense, or embed the Model weights in any third-party marketplace, bundled hardware package, or commercial distribution channel without prior written consent from Nimbus Labs.
```
marina: They also request that any export control filtering be implemented on the client side.
legal-bot: Running compatibility scan vs Redwood marketplace requirements and SI channel policy. Flag: hosting prohibition conflicts with our managed-delivery and marketplace hosting model.
ajay: Two options: 1) Ask for limited hosting carve-out for authorized marketplaces/SIs with technical safeguards (ephemeral signed URLs, region ACLs, watermarking). 2) If they refuse, offer a managed-proxy model: we call their hosted API on behalf of customers and charge for orchestration, but no weights stored. This may be worse for latency/cost.
tom_s: Managed-proxy is feasible but has scaling concerns. NLX-3 has high memory use; proxying every customer request increases outbound egress costs and could affect latency SLOs.
marina: Nimbus said they don't want downstream resellers repackaging weights. They might accept a carve-out limited to "authorized channel partners" and "marketplace SKUs where weights remain controlled by Nimbus or are encrypted for authorized hosters."
sylvie: Marketing: please don't plan any joint launch until the license is clarified. We need a statement permitting marketplace listing before we create co-marketing assets.
elaine_mktg: noted. we'll hold the blog and joint webinar dates. keep us posted.
ajay: Draft ask: 1) carve-out to allow Redwood and authorized channel partners to host or cache weights when used to deliver marketplace SKUs or Dedicated managed images; 2) technical requirements: server-side encryption (CMK), signed short-lived download URLs, access logging, and tamper-proof provenance tags; 3) export-control: Nimbus to provide embargo list and acceptable geofencing method.
marina: I'll send that today and include a one-paragraph justification for Nimbus security concerns (we'll propose controls).
legal-bot: Suggested contract language ready 12: short carve-out clause + audit rights + indemnity cap note. Want me to attach?
ajay: Yes attach suggested clause. Also loop in compliance for export controls.
tom_s: If they insist on client-side filtering only, we'd ask for proof-of-concept traffic filtering and an operator runbook. Otherwise we can't comply for Hosted API mode.
sylvie: Also add a co-announcement embargo: 72 hours pre-publish notice and approval on quoted benchmarks.
marina: Pinged Nimbus: @nimbus-legal and @nimbus-ops can you confirm whether you will accept a limited hosting carve-out for authorized marketplace/Dedicated delivery with the technical controls above? Also please share your export-control embargo list and whether you require client-side geofencing only. ETA?
marina: cc @elaine_mktg for timeline.
elaine_mktg: thanks all :raised_hands:
